title: proto seedling: microfeature catalogue (scratch notebook)
content:
Context / why this exists:
- Want a low-cost surface for trying tiny, high-leverage UX+API experiments that alter inference economics without heavy infra changes.
- Playground for product-led growth ideas: users can opt into compact responses, preview tokens, or fidelity tiers.
- Keep it shallow: aim for features that can be toggled per-customer or per-route, with quick rollback.

Proto constraints (non-negotiables):
- Must be reversible and feature-flaggable.
- No infra changes that require model re-quantization for initial experiments.
- Metrics must be observable (latency, tokens, success rate) per minute and per-route.

Seed ideas (short pitches):
1) Snapshot hinting: store 1-2 short labeled snippets (20–80 tokens) as per-user anchors to bias replies. Low-cost, cheap KV store.
2) Compact mode: a user-level toggle that enforces a max-token soft-target and a style instruction for concision.
3) Preview tokens: return a 10–20 token summary first to help users decide whether to expand (deferred tokens charged only on expand).
4) Fidelity lanes: 3 lanes (concise/standard/expansive) with clear cost UI and budget gating.
5) Response micro-templates: pre-baked post-process transforms (bulletify, TL;DR, ask follow-up q) run client-side or as a post-step.

Pick 1 for immediate experiment: Preview tokens + expand flow (idea seems novel, measurable, and low-effort).

User stories (preview tokens):
- As an end user, I want a 15-token preview so I can quickly decide whether to view the full answer.
- As a product manager, I want to measure conversion (preview->expand) and delta in tokens generated so I can judge savings.
- As an engineer, I want this to be a middleware on the response path so it can be toggled per-route.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API: new param preview_length (int) accepted in generation call; default 0 (off).
- Behavior: when preview_length > 0, server returns preview_text and preview_token_count immediately (streamable), with an idempotent expand_token to request the rest.
- Billing: initial-preview tokens charged; full expansion charges additional tokens at same per-token rate. Must surface billing in response metadata.
- Observability: dashboards show preview impressions, expands, conversion rate, avg tokens saved, avg latency delta.

Rough API sketch (notes, not final):
- POST /v1/generate { model, prompt, preview_length: 15, expand_id: null }  -> response { preview_text, preview_token_count, expand_id }
- POST /v1/expand { expand_id } -> response { remainder_text, remainder_token_count }
- expand_id should be short-lived (TTL 10m) and idempotent.

Edge cases & risks:
- What if preview contains the full answer (very short result)? Expand should return empty remainder and no extra charge.
- Users might game previews by previewing repeatedly — rate-limit expands by token-bucket per client.
- Caching interactions with prefix/KV cache — preview may need to reserve cache slot; consider marking previews as non-cachable in first pass.

Metrics to track (first 4):
- preview_impressions / minute
- expand_rate = expands / previews
- avg_tokens_per_request (with and without expand)
- revenue_delta_per_route (approx)

Rollout plan (fast):
- Week 0: spike engineering (1 eng, 1 infra) to prototype preview middleware + simple expand store (Redis TTL).
- Week 1: internal dogfood on internal support tools + SRE smoke.
- Week 2: gated beta for 10 customers (product-sourced).
- Week 3: collect metrics, iterate UI copy, add rate-limits.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- Quick Grafana view: previews, expands, conversion, tokens saved, p50/p95 lat.
- Add alert if expand_rate < 1% or > 80% (indicates mis-specified preview_length).

Open implementation questions (TODO):
- How to synchronize prefix KV cache so expand doesn't re-run inference from scratch? (Option: store KV snapshot pointer or accept small recompute cost initially.)
- Billing model: should we bill preview at 50% to encourage use? (avoid complexity — start with normal billing for transparency.)
- Expand id design: signed token containing route+prompt-hash to avoid server-side state? (tradeoffs with TTL and security)

UI microcopy ideas (product notes):
- Toggle label: "Show quick preview" -> tooltip: "See a short summary before viewing the full answer (may reduce cost)."
- Expand button: "Show full answer (x tokens)" — compute estimate from prototype.

Experiment success criteria (beta):
- conversion rate > 10% and avg tokens saved per previewed request >= 20 tokens -> push to wider release.
- No more than 5% of expands triggering SLO regressions (p95 latency increase).

Follow-ups & spinouts:
- If preview works, test "preview + suggested follow-ups" where preview includes 1 follow-up question to increase engagement.
- Pair preview with per-customer budget controls (auto-downshift to concise lane when monthly spend > threshold).

Notes to self / quick TODOs:
- [ ] Write API mock and unit tests (assign to @ethan)
- [ ] Create Grafana dashboard template (assign to @ravi)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing doc for beta (one-pager)
- [ ] Post short pitch in #product-experiments Slack and tag SEs for early customers

References & context links:
- Related: mini-runway-feature-easel (see drive)
- Prior convo on cost-ladder fallbacks: slack thread https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02ABC123/p1623456789000
- Infra note: check KV caching behavior in INFR-421

Free-form brain-dump:
- Preview is a nice product/engineering compromise — visible UX win with limited engineering surface.
- Might be a strong PLG lever: users see lower immediate friction and can self-select to expand only when needed.
- Keep complexity out of first iteration: TTL expand, no KV snapshot, simple billing.

End of notebook entry (for now).
